{{Top}}
[[File:PazaakBroonTersDotonHet-KotOR2.jpg|thumb|right|250px|[[Broon Ters]] and [[Doton Het]] play pazaak.]]
'''Pazaak''', a game dating back to [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Old Republic]] times, was a popular card game in which the goal was to come closest to 20 without going over. The player with the highest score less than or equal to 20 won the round, and the player who won three rounds won the match. A round in which the two players tied was not counted.

==Gameplay==
[[File:Pazaaktables.jpg|thumb|300px|During the time of the [[Mandalorian Wars]] and the [[Jedi Civil War]], pazaak rooms were found in almost any [[Cantina/Legends|cantina]] in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].]]
Pazaak had two different decks. The main (or "table") deck was composed of cards numbered 1&ndash;10. (The total cards in this deck were unbound, though it tended to have four of each number.) There was also one side deck for each player in the game. The players themselves assembled these decks, which had to have exactly ten cards.<ref name="KOTOR">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''</ref>

At the beginning of the game, each player would randomly select four cards from their side deck, making up their Hand. Each player drew a card from the main deck. Then the first turn of the first player would start. The player would draw a card from the main deck and play it on the table. After that, the player could either place a card down from their hand or end their turn. Only one hand card could be played per turn, and no more cards were ever drawn from the side deck.<ref name="KOTOR" />

When ending their turn, the player had two options:

'''End Turn''': If the player ended their turn, they had to draw a new card from the main deck at the start of the next turn. This was repeated until either they stood, went bust, filled the table, or reached a score of exactly 20.<ref name="KOTOR" />

'''Stand''': If the player stood, they kept their current sum until the end of the set and did not play any other cards. The opponent, however, could continue playing cards unless he had chosen to stand as well. Getting a sum of 20 automatically caused a player to stand.<ref name="KOTOR" />

Once their turn was over, the next player played their turn in the same manner. Play alternated between the two players until someone won the set.<ref name="KOTOR" />

The winner of the set was then the first player for the next set. In the case of a tie, whoever was not the first player for the tied set was the first player for the next set.<ref name="KOTOR" />

==The cards==
Pazaak used two decks:

The '''Main Deck''' consisted of four sets of cards numbered 1 to 10.<ref name="KOTOR" />

The '''Side Deck''' consisted of ten unique cards the player chose before the match. At the start of each game, four of these cards were chosen at random for the player to keep in their hand and play at any time they desired.<ref name="KOTOR" />

The side deck also had a variety of cards, and each deck was unique to the player in that they could purchase different types of cards throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] and choose whichever ones he preferred to keep in their hand. There were two types of such cards: Plus and Minus cards, blue and red,<ref name="KOTOR" /> and Advanced cards, which were gold. Main Deck cards were green,<ref name="KOTOR II">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''</ref> or in some older cases gold.<ref name="KOTOR" />

'''Plus Cards''' were blue cards that added the indicated value to a player's total when played. The value of the cards ranged from 1 to 6 points.<ref name="KOTOR" />

'''Minus Cards''' were red cards similar to the plus cards, but instead, they subtracted their value from the player's total. They also ranged from 1 to 6.<ref name="KOTOR" />

'''Plus or Minus Cards (+/&minus;)''' were essentially a combination of the two; the player could choose upon play whether they wanted to add the number or subtract it from their hand. These were the most expensive and highly valued cards. They also ranged from 1 to 6.<ref name="KOTOR" />

The '''+/&minus; 1 or 2 Card''' was a +/&minus; card whose value could be changed to between 1 and 2.

'''Flip Cards''' were advanced cards that changed the positive sign of all cards in play matching their own values, to negative. For example, if a player played a 2&4 flip card, all the 2s and 4s on the table would become &minus;2s and &minus;4s. These cards were only available as 2&4 and 3&6.<ref name="KOTOR II" />

The '''Double Card''' was a rare card that doubled the value of the last played card. For example, if one flipped over 2, then a 9, they could play the double card, making the 9 an 18, thus adding up to 20. A player known as [[Mebla Dule]] gave the [[Meetra Surik|Jedi Exile]] this card after being beaten on [[Telos IV]].<ref name="KOTOR II" />

The '''Tiebreaker Card''' was a scarce card that acted like a +/&minus;1 card, but the player who played the tiebreaker card would win in the event of a tie. A tiebreaker card was owned by the being on [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]] known as [[the Champ]] until he gave it to the Exile after losing his position to the Jedi.<ref name="KOTOR II" />

The Side Deck was often the key to victory, as, without their hand, a player relied solely on luck to win the match. Therefore, a player would have to conserve their cards, as the four side deck cards would have to last them through the entire match.<ref name="KOTOR" />

==Winning the game==
There were four ways to win the set:

By outscoring: After both players chose to stand, the player with the score closest to but not over 20 would win.<ref name="KOTOR" />

By going bust: If a player ended their turn with a score over 20, they were said to "bust," and the other player won.<ref name="KOTOR" />

By filling the table: In some rare occasions, if a player placed 9 cards on the table without busting, the player would automatically win if their score ended up being 20 or under.<ref name="KOTOR II" />

By using the tiebreaker card: A golden tiebreaker card, when used last, brought victory to the user if both players had the same score.<ref name="KOTOR II" />

When a set tied, no one got the point for the set, and a new set was played. The first player to win three sets won the game, and whatever was being wagered.<ref name="KOTOR" />

==Areas of play==
As a card game, pazaak could be played just about anywhere, but the most popular places to play were on ships during hyperspace transit,<ref name="KOTOR II" /> at the local cantina,<ref name="KOTOR" /> or at particular areas designated for play, such as the [[Pazaak Den]] in the Nar Shaddaa [[Refugee Sector]].<ref name="KOTOR II" />

==Alternate rules==
When played just to pass time (not for money), pazaak players used [[Republic Senate rules]], in which nothing was bet, and no one came out on top. This variation was mockingly named for the perception that the senate would continually debate an issue without taking risks and without real world consequences.<ref name="KOTOR II" /> There was also a Nar Shaddaa version, in which the players removed clothing or kept a blaster ready.<ref>:''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''
::'''Atton''': "''Why do I play pazaak? All right. I'll show you.''"
::'''Exile''': "''I don't want to play pazaak.''"
::'''Atton''': "''We're not playing for credits. We're playing for something else. Are you going to play or not?''"
::'''Exile''': "''This better not be using Nar Shaddaa rules.''"
::'''Atton''': "''(to Female Exile) Nope, our clothes are gonna stay on.''"
::'''Atton''': "''(to Male Exile) Nope, blasters stay in their holsters.''"</ref>

==Alternate uses==
Like all games, pazaak quickly became a form of gambling, and most players in the galaxy wouldn't even consider playing with someone before discussing the wager.<ref name="KOTOR" /> However, people still played "Republic Senate" rules for fun.<ref name="KOTOR II" /> A [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] man known as [[Atton Rand]] often used pazaak to shield his thoughts: by concentrating on a theoretical game or various strategies, he made it more difficult for anyone attempting to read his mind to see deeper than the game. He taught this skill to the Jedi Exile, [[Meetra Surik]].<ref name="KOTOR II" /> 

Rand also used the exclamation "Pure Pazaak", for a desired result.<ref name="KOTOR II" /> 

==Behind the scenes==
Pazaak is a minigame created for the [[2003]] [[roleplaying game]] ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]'',<ref name="KOTOR" /> and was also included in its [[2004]] sequel, ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''.<ref name="KOTOR II" />

The "filling the table" win condition only applies in ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]'';<ref name="KOTOR II" /> in the first game, filling the table would merely count as an automatic stand, and the rules of the game are applied as normal following that.<ref name="KOTOR" /> Filling the table is mentioned in the rules section, in completed quests (part 2 of 2), after asking [[Atton Rand|Atton]] on the ''[[Ebon Hawk]]'' to go over the rules for you.<ref name="KOTOR II" />

It is similar in principle to the real world game of [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blackjack Blackjack], where players attempt to get as close as possible to a score of 21 without going over. Blackjack is also frequently played in casinos.
